::: {.why}
The cross-sectional regression run period by period is the standard way risk premia get estimated in this field, and its whole point is a dependence structure you already correct for elsewhere.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Describe the two stages of Fama-MacBeth and say precisely which source of dependence the procedure handles.
- Report a risk premium estimate with Fama-MacBeth standard errors and compare against the naive pooled version.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>55 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [30 min]{.task-min} Run it both ways on the 25 portfolios with linearmodels: a pooled panel regression of returns on exposures, and the Fama-MacBeth two-stage procedure. Report the same coefficient with both standard errors and state the ratio between them.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [25 min]{.task-min} Say what the correction is doing: the cross-sectional residuals are correlated within a period because everything moves with the market, so pooling treats correlated observations as independent. Write the one-sentence version, then add the Shanken correction note, which accounts for the betas themselves being estimated.
:::
